title: v1/chat.completions parity: canonicalize params, robust stream framing, toolcall envelope, unified logprob schema
author: Neha Kapoor
description:
Context: We need closer parity with OpenAI's /v1/chat.completions for customers migrating from OpenAI-style clients and for downstream SDKs that assume certain parameter behaviors. This PR harmonizes parameter semantics (temperature/top_p/stop/stream), stabilizes streaming framing for partial response reassembly, defines a compact envelope for tool/function call messages, and normalizes logprob/stop output to a single canonical schema so downstream evals and quality checks don't need special-case parsing.

Motivation: Previously, subtle mismatches in param coercion (e.g., falsy stop vs. explicit null), inconsistent handling of role aliases, and varying streaming frame shapes caused customer regressions during migration and brittle SDK logic. Additionally, toolcall outputs were emitted as ad-hoc fragments which complicated function routing in edge cases and retry scenarios.

What this PR does (summary):
- Canonicalizes chat params: explicit null vs omitted, numeric coercion for temperature and top_p, and whitelist/aliasing for role names (user/system/assistant/tool).
- Stabilizes stream framing: introduces a small frame header for every chunk that carries a sequence id, frame type (delta|tool|done|heartbeat), and optional json-mode marker; keeps backwards-compatible fallback parsing for old clients.
- Tool/function call envelope: emits a single well-formed tool-call event when a tool is invoked; the envelope contains tool_name, args (string|json), and optional provenance headers. This replaces earlier multi-chunk tool call patterns.
- Unified logprob schema: stop reasons, token logprobs, and token offsets are now embedded under response.logprobs with consistent keys: tokens, token_logprobs, token_offsets, stop_reason. Old fields are still emitted as deprecated aliases for one release.
- Response shaping: structured output for 'json_mode' requests is enforced: top-level message.content is either a plain string or a JSON-encoded object with content_type header. Streaming will emit partial JSON fragments under the same envelope type to aid reassembly.

Files changed (high level):
- runtime/streaming/frame_protocol.go (new framing + parser)
- runtime/streaming/frame_protocol_test.go (parser/unit tests covering reassembly & heartbeat)
- api/compat/chatv1/param_canonicalizer.go (param coercion and alias handling)
- api/compat/chatv1/response_normalizer.go (output shaping and logprob schema)
- api/compat/chatv1/toolcall_envelope.go (single-toolcall emitter)
- sdk/js/src/streaming/reader.ts (compat parsing of new frames, fallback to legacy)
- sdk/python/redwood/chatv1_client.py (parameter acceptance and docs)
- docs/openai_compat/chatv1_migration.md (migration notes and examples)
- tests/e2e/chatv1_migration_test.go (end-to-end scenarios)
- perf/canaries/chat_streaming_latency.yaml (adjusted canary config to account for header overhead)
- examples/chatv1-toolcall/ (updated sample showing tool envelope usage)

Commits (summary):
- 1a2b3c: introduce canonicalizer and initial unit tests
- 4d5e6f: implement framing protocol + parser and reassembly logic
- 7g8h9i: toolcall envelope emitter + SDK parsers for JS/Python
- a1b2c3: normalize logprob schema and add deprecation aliases
- d4e5f6: docs, migration guide and examples
- f7g8h9: canary/perf tweak and CI test adjustments

Review notes / decisions:
- We added a tiny header (3 fields) before payload to make reassembly deterministic under concurrent chunk streams. Hardware/throughput impact measured at +0.6% token overhead in our perf lab for small payloads, negligible at typical batch sizes.
- To preserve backwards compatibility, the JS and Python SDKs will continue to accept the legacy frame stream; new header-aware parsing is preferred when available (sdk negotiates by attempting header parse and falling back).
- The unified logprob schema intentionally groups stop reasons under response.logprobs.stop_reason to make automatic eval tooling easier. We emit deprecated fields response.tokens and response.token_logprobs for one release and will remove them after SDK upgrades are broadly available.

Testing performed:
- Unit tests for param canonicalization edge cases (empty lists, null vs omitted, role aliasing).
- Streaming reassembly fuzz tests that simulate interleaved tool-call and assistant frames.
- Integration tests: migration scenarios (OpenAI-like client sending top_p as string, stop as empty array, streaming toggled mid-request).
- Manual QA: ran example customers' prompts where older clients previously mis-merging tool outputs.

Backward compatibility & migration:
- Clients that upgrade SDKs gain new parsing and deprecation warnings.
- Servers using custom parser need to accept the small header; a fallback branch is documented in the migration guide.
- Operators can enable a compatibility flag in deploy config to allow legacy-only streaming for 30 days while dependent services upgrade.

Related work: ENG-1942 (param parity initiative), ENG-1978 (streaming reliability), SUP-889 (customer incident where stop arrays were ignored). This PR consolidates many smaller fixes into a cohesive interface to lower migration cost.

Release notes (short): Canonicalize v1/chat.completions params, stabilize streaming frames with a compact header for reliable reassembly, emit a single well-formed toolcall envelope for function calls, and normalize logprob/stop schema. SDKs updated (JS/Python) to parse the new frames and honor deprecation aliases.

Why this PR is different: Unlike previous incremental PRs that tackled parameter or streaming issues in isolation, this change intentionally coordinates runtime, API compat, SDKs, and docs so customer migrations are predictable and reversible. It prioritizes a single canonical output shape for logprobs and toolcalls to reduce downstream parsing complexity.

Merge outcome: squashed and merged after 2 approvals and one CI flake rerun.
review_comments: Ethan Li: Overall looks great. Two questions: 1) Did you consider using varint encoding for the header to save bytes? 2) Can we avoid emitting deprecated aliases in perf path?

Neha Kapoor: Varint considered but added CPU/decode complexity; header is fixed 3-field little-endian for simplicity and deterministic parse. Deprecated aliases are not emitted on 'fast-path' quantized executor to keep perf stable.
Sofia Martinez: Please add migration snippet for top_p passed as string in docs (example client).
Neha Kapoor: Added example and unit tests covering top_p string coercion.
Oliver Chen: Unit tests flaked on CI once (streaming fuzz test). Is that stable now?
Neha Kapoor: Increased timeouts and added deterministic seeds; re-ran CI pipeline and all streaming tests passed.
QA (Priya Das): Verified end-to-end sample with external OpenAI-like client; toolcall reassembly and logprob shape validated.
Security (Rajiv Nair): Static review — no new surface, toolcall provenance headers must be treated as untrusted by consumers. Added note to docs.
SRE (Lena Hsu): Perf canary noted small latency increase; acceptable. Recommend monitoring 99th percentile for first week.
Product (Marta Kovacs): Approved for GA; migration docs clear enough for customers to act.
release_notes: Canonicalize v1/chat.completions params and streaming framing; introduce single toolcall envelope; unified logprob/stop schema; SDK updates for JS/Python. Deprecated aliases emitted for one release.
notes_for_operators: Operators: enable"compat_streaming_v1" flag to continue serving legacy header-less frames during migration window. Monitor perf canary dashboard for +p95 latency regressions and disable legacy-only mode after clients upgrade.
changelog_entry: API: chatv1 parameter canonicalization and streaming stability; toolcall envelope and unified logprob schema (sdk updates included).
